NEW DELHI: The Delhi government has declared November 16, 2026, a public holiday on account of Pratihar Shashthi or Surya Shashthi, popularly known as Chhath Puja. The holiday will apply to all government offices, autonomous bodies and Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) functioning under the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi. The notification was issued by the General Administration Department on November 9, 2026, with the approval of the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi. The order will be published in the Delhi Gazette, Part IV (Extraordinary). Delhi government holiday notification
 According to the official notification, November 16 falls on a Monday and has been declared a holiday for the specified government establishments across Delhi. The notification was issued by Pradeep Tayal, Joint Secretary, General Administration Department, under file number 53/876/GAD/CN/2026/6376-6418. Copies of the order have been forwarded to various government departments, ministries, administrative offices and municipal authorities for information and necessary action. Chhath Puja holiday 2026 in Delhi
 Chhath Puja, also observed as Pratihar Shashthi or Surya Shashthi, is an important festival dedicated to the worship of the Sun God. Devotees observe rituals and offer prayers during sunrise and sunset as part of the celebrations. The November 16 holiday specifically covers government offices, autonomous bodies and PSUs under the Delhi government, as mentioned in the notification. Employees and residents can refer to the official government notification for details regarding the applicable holiday arrangements.
